project:
## Overview

Safe Shield (also called GuptAI by the team; final name is open) is a Chrome Manifest V3 browser extension that protects people using cloud AI with private documents. It detects and redacts sensitive content locally before the user submits a prompt, then lets the user review the redacted version and restore originals locally.

## Problem statement

Hacktoberfest Hack Day, problem statement #3: “PII redaction for Indian documents and languages”. People paste documents containing names, IDs, and account numbers into cloud chatbots. The product helps anyone using cloud AI with private documents.

The slide’s “What to build” box discusses news claims and source verification and appears to belong to a different problem statement. The team follows the PII project description; see D-001.

## Requirements

Core features:

- Automatic PII detection.
- Smart redaction with stable, typed placeholders.
- Pre-submission protection before text leaves the page.
- Privacy shield toggle.
- Detection preview before sending.
- Local restoration of original text.
- Privacy dashboard with counts only.
- Indian language support, including Hindi/Hinglish where feasible.
- Clean, modern UI.

First supported platform: ChatGPT at `chatgpt.com` and `chat.openai.com`.

Delivery is time-boxed to six hours, with feature freeze at about hour 5.5. Tier 1 is must-have, Tier 2 is only if stable, and Tier 3 is after the window.

## Privacy rules

- All detection runs locally.
- Never send unredacted text to any external service.
- Fail closed: if detection or redaction throws, block the send and warn the user.
- Show “Active” only if the composer is found and interception hooks are attached.
- Keep the placeholder-to-original map in memory or `chrome.storage.session` only.
- Persist dashboard counts only, never detected values.
- Gemma is optional Tier 3; prefer local execution (for example, through Ollama), and only provide already-redacted text. The core project requires no model API.

## Tech stack

Chrome Manifest V3, plain JavaScript, no bundler, and no runtime dependencies. Development dependencies may support formatting, linting, and tests. Any optional Gemma integration is Tier 3 only.

## Architecture and data flow

`type -> intercept send -> detect locally -> redact -> preview -> send redacted -> update counts`

Content scripts target the ChatGPT composer. Since MV3 content scripts cannot use ES module imports without a bundler, files in `src/core`, `src/shared`, and `src/content` attach exports to `globalThis.SafeShield` and use a guarded `module.exports` for Node tests.

## Contracts

- `detect(text) -> [{ type, start, end, value }]`
- `redact(text) -> { redactedText, entities: [{ placeholder, type, original }], counts }`
- `restore(text, entities) -> string`
- Placeholder form: `[TYPE_n]`, numbered per type; the same value receives the same placeholder.
- Storage keys: `enabled` (boolean) and `stats` (counts per type only).

## Ownership map

- M1: detection engine (`src/core`) and tests.
- M2: platform integration (`src/content`).
- M3: UI/UX (`src/ui`) and assets.
- M4: foundation, data, and docs (`manifest.json`, `src/shared`, `src/dashboard`, `src/background`, `docs`, `.github`, and scripts).

## Conventions

- Branch names: `feat/<member>-<task>`.
- Use conventional commit prefixes such as `feat:`, `fix:`, `test:`, and `chore:`.
- Keep pull requests small.
- Review pairing: M1 <-> M2 and M3 <-> M4.
- Keep per-member history in `docs/changelog/member-N.md`; generated master files must not be edited by hand.

## Open questions

- Final product name: “Safe Shield” or “GuptAI”.

decisions.title: Chrome MV3 with plain JavaScript
decisions.body:
**Decision:** Use Chrome Manifest V3, plain JavaScript, no bundler, and the `globalThis.SafeShield` namespace with a guarded CommonJS export for tests.
**Why:** MV3 content scripts cannot use ES module imports without a bundler, and the product must run directly from source.
**Alternatives:** Add a bundler or use module imports in content scripts.
**Impact:** Keep source files compatible with direct script loading and Node tests.

decisions.title: Local deterministic detection; optional Gemma later
decisions.body:
**Decision:** Use local regex and checksum detection for the core; consider Gemma only as optional Tier 3 with already-redacted input.
**Why:** Core privacy must not depend on an external model service.
**Alternatives:** Send prompts to a hosted model for detection.
**Impact:** Core operation requires no model API; any optional AI path must enforce redacted-only input.

decisions.title: Per-member logs and generated master files
decisions.body:
**Decision:** Keep append-only per-member logs and generate master changelog/state files.
**Why:** Separate ownership reduces concurrent edit conflicts while preserving a single current handoff.
**Alternatives:** Have all members edit one shared changelog and state file.
**Impact:** Edit `docs/changelog/member-N.md`; never hand-edit generated master files.

latestPerMember.body:
**Prompt:** fix: remove Verhoeff gate from Aadhaar detection
**What changed:**
- Removed Verhoeff checksum requirement from isValidAadhaar() in validators.js; now accepts any 12-digit number starting with 2-9 (structural check only). Verhoeff functions kept and still exported for optional use.
- Updated tests/validators.test.js: 'rejects false positives' test now asserts that structural Aadhaar (234567890123) IS accepted, and still asserts starts-with-0/1 and wrong-length are rejected.
- Updated tests/detector.test.js: 'false positives' test updated to remove badAadhaar case and adds a positive assertion that a structural Aadhaar IS now detected.
  **Files:** `src/core/validators.js` (modified), `tests/validators.test.js` (modified), `tests/detector.test.js` (modified)
  **Status:** done
  **Tasks:** T1-03
  **Decisions:** none
  **Notes for others:** Verhoeff is intentionally dropped from detection — over-redacting is safer than missing a real Aadhaar. If stricter precision is needed later, add it as an opt-in setting, not a default gate.
  **Next:** Implement T1-01 (phone detector) and T1-02 (email detector) if not already complete; then T1-05 (redact() with consistent placeholders).

latestPerMember.body:
**Prompt:** fix: add SS_SEND_REDACTED handler in main.js
**What changed:**
- Added SS_SEND_REDACTED case to the chrome.runtime.onMessage listener in main.js; guards against disabled/no-composer states, reads composer text, runs redact(), writes redacted text back into composer, shows preview-modal, and replies synchronously with {ok:true} so the popup feedback works immediately.
- Cancel action restores original text; Send action calls composer.submit(adapter); no_pii case replies with reason:'no_pii'.
  **Files:** `src/content/main.js` (modified)
  **Status:** done
  **Tasks:** none
  **Decisions:** none
  **Notes for others:** The SS_SEND_REDACTED handler does NOT run the full fail-closed interceptor path (no final PII re-check before submit). M2 should add a final detect() safety guard before composer.submit if time allows.
  **Next:** Test the full flow in live Chrome — open ChatGPT, type PII, click extension icon, click Send Redacted, confirm preview modal appears.

**Prompt:** feat: add Send Redacted button to popup
**What changed:**
- Added a "Send Redacted" full-width button with shield icon to popup.html, placed above the Privacy Dashboard footer link in its own .send-redacted-section.

  **Tasks:** T1-11

  **Notes for others:** Content script (main.js / interceptor.js, owned by M2) must handle the SS_SEND_REDACTED message type and reply with {ok:true}, {ok:false, reason:'no_pii'}, {ok:false, reason:'disabled'}, or {ok:false, message:'...'} for the popup feedback to work end-to-end.
